Bug.Description: Recursive fault on system check (critical or lower) due to poor DIAG X'288' hercules patch
Bug.Behavior: If any subsystem of the kernel triggers a system check (critical or lower), kernel will recursively fault with Operation Exception, and/or trigger a restart (due to misconfigured timebomb)
Bug.Solution: Patches Hercules DIAG X'288' Patch to be more robust (also mirror linux)

Bug.Description: IRQ descriptor table slot-number allocation mismatch causes all SCOMS-managed IRQ dispatch to silently fail, posting no handlers for any external interrupt (clock comparator, CPU timer, IPI, etc.)
Bug.Behavior:
irq_register() called g_irq_table.alloc() which pulled an arbitrary free-list slot index S, populating m_slots[S] with the handler. irq_dispatch() and find_raw() look up slots by the IRQ vector number V (so m_slots[V]), which remained with ko.id == KOBJECT_ID_INVALID. The lookup returned nullptr and the handler was never invoked.
Consequence: ext.cxxm routed every external interrupt through the IRQ table (instead of direct fast paths), so clock comparator events, CPU timer ticks, timing alerts, service signals, and IPI vectors all produced zero dispatch work. Without timer-driven scheduler ticks the BSP stopped advancing, and APs entering sched_init_ap simultaneously raced raw PMM allocations with no scheduler heartbeat, yielding nondeterministic PMM free-list corruption (assert_allocatable_frame with frame_owner::stack, order 2), deadlocks (254/255 progress stall), or undefined spin-wait hangs.
Bug.Solution:
Introduced kobject_table::alloc_at(u32 id) which claims a specific slot index by unlinking it from the SCOMS free-list rather than taking an arbitrary slot from the free-list head. irqdesc::irq_register() now calls alloc_at(irq) so the irq_desc for vector V always occupies m_slots[V], making find_raw(V) reach the correct descriptor.
Additional benefit: alloc_at() is robust against reuse of a slot by a different IRQ vector — if m_slots[id].ko.id != KOBJECT_ID_INVALID, the call returns already_locked, which replaces the silent double-registration that existed before.

Bug.Description: __schedule early-return path leaves the re-picked strand with substate==runnable instead of substate==running.
Bug.Behavior:
In sched::schedule() the prev strand is enqueued (or kept runnable) at L423-L437 — its substate is set to sched_substate::runnable. When select_next() then picks the same strand again (next == prev), the function takes the early-return branch (L477-L481) and skips the next->substate = sched_substate::running transition at L494.
Consequence: any strand that yields and is immediately re-picked retains substate==runnable even though it IS the running strand. This was exposed by dom_op::strand_query_state (user/init/init.S Test 57) which read the primary strand's substate from inside a running SVC handler and observed substate==1 (runnable) instead of substate==2 (running). Beyond the test failure, the bug silently corrupts any scheduler introspection or migration logic that consults strand.substate on the running strand to decide whether the CPU is currently committed.
Bug.Solution: Set next->substate = sched_substate::running before the early-return from the next==prev branch in __schedule. This is the same transition the long-form handoff path performs at L494; the early-return was simply missing it.

Bug.Description: cap::acquire syscall retained the removed forgeable type/id ABI instead of accepting a nucleus-issued source capability token
Bug.Behavior: user/init passed cap_type, domain id, and requested rights to cap::acquire. The nucleus interpreted the first argument as an opaque token, so the reconstructed value failed capability-slot generation and ownership validation.
Bug.Solution: Bootstrap now supplies an all-rights nucleus-issued source token through the preserved init ABI register. cap::acquire derives only from that token, while the init tests use the opaque token for admin, map, and delegate derivation.

Bug.Description: Domain names retained temporary user-buffer pointers and secondary strands retained SCOMS parent dependencies during teardown
Bug.Behavior: The domain-create syscall passed a stack-local copied name to domain_create(), leaving domain::name dangling. Later teardown logs printed empty or corrupted names. Domain destruction also released secondary strand slots without detaching them from the domain, so the final domain release could fail with live dependents.
Bug.Solution: Domains now own a bounded inline name buffer and copy names into it during creation. Secondary strand teardown detaches each strand from its domain before releasing its SCOMS slot.

Bug.Description: Domain teardown discarded the VM address-space pointer before releasing its SCOMS object
Bug.Behavior: vm_destroy_space() cleared vm_space.address_space_object after removing regions. domain_destroy() therefore skipped the address-space object release, leaving the domain object with a live SCOMS dependent and causing dom::destroy to return generic::invalid_arg.
Bug.Solution: VM teardown now leaves the address-space object reference for domain_destroy() to release after all region and memory-object children have been detached. Domain teardown also drains IPC endpoints, policy registrations, and named services owned by the dying domain.

Bug.Description: vm_region alloc_region double-constructed the slot, wiping the SCOMS id assigned by kobject_table::alloc
Bug.Behavior: alloc_region() called ::new(static_cast(rgn)) vm_region{} after g_region_table.alloc() had already default-constructed the slot and initialised ko.id via ko.initialize(slot, type). The placement-new zero-initialised the storage, clearing ko.id back to ~0U. Capabilities issued against such a region therefore failed lookup_kobject() (cap_issue returned generic::not_found) and every operation that relied on a valid region ko.id — shm_export, lazy revocation, region teardown — was broken.
Bug.Solution: Removed the redundant placement-new and the ko.type reassignment. alloc_region now only fills in the user-visible fields (va_start, va_end, prot, flags, backing, phys_base) and activates the embryo ref. ko.id and ko.type are preserved from kobject_table::alloc().
